title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
gist: The US has gone 10 months without a space tourism mission as Blue Origin paused New Shepard, SpaceX ended Dragon free-flyers and Virgin Galactic's Unity retired. Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class ship, Apeiron, is moving to Spaceport America for testing ahead of a targeted early Q2 2027 commercial debut, with the stock near $2.50 versus a 2021 peak of $1,118.

insights.claim: The US has gone 10 months without a space tourism mission.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: The sector has effectively stalled after the 2021 euphoria.
insights.quote: So we are now 10 months, and counting, without a space tourism mission in the United States.

insights.claim: Berger argues Blue Origin has effectively abandoned New Shepard: its last flight was in January, the program is 'paused,' and its engineering teams now support New Glenn and Blue Moon.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Blue Origin's capital is reallocated to orbital and lunar programs, exiting suborbital tourism.
insights.quote: The program was subsequently “paused,” but let’s be real. Blue Origin has moved on.

insights.claim: SpaceX flew its final Dragon free-flyer mission, Fram2, in April 2025; the remaining non-NASA station missions will likely carry government astronauts, Dragon will then be retired, and there is no credible timeline for Starship to fly humans from Earth.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Private orbital tourism has no near-term vehicle in the US.
insights.quote: There is no credible timeline for SpaceX’s Starship to fly humans into space from Earth.

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic planned two Delta-class ships in service by 2026 but has none in service; the first, named Apeiron, is only now moving from Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Virgin Galactic has already slipped its own fleet timeline.
insights.quote: It planned to bring two of these Delta-class ships into service by the year 2026. Of course, it is now 2026, and there are no Delta-class ships in service.

insights.claim: Apeiron still needs avionics and flight software completion, ground tests, captive carry tests on VMS Eve, a drop test and a powered test flight above 80 km before commercial service.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Several test milestones remain, each a possible slip point.

insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Revenue restart is likely mid-to-late 2027, not early.
insights.quote: But it seems plausible that Apeiron may begin flying paying customers on suborbital space tourism missions over the next 12 to 18 months.
